articles.title: Mysterious brain activity under anesthesia challenges what we know about consciousness

articles.title: Eating late at night linked to up to 30% higher risk of liver disease
articles.summary: Eating late at night could be putting your liver at risk, according to a large study led by Oregon Health & Science University. Researchers analyzed data from nearly 200,000 people and found that those who regularly ate after dinner or around bedtime had a 20% to 30% higher risk of liver disease, including fatty liver disease and cirrhosis.

articles.title: Rare study reveals a striking divide inside an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain
articles.summary: A rare examination of an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain revealed that regions cleared of amyloid plaques had remarkably little of the harmful tau buildup associated with memory loss, while neighboring areas showed extensive damage. The discovery suggests that removing amyloid may have lasting protective effects and could help slow Alzheimer’s progression, especially when treatment begins early.

articles.title: A 47-year study reveals the age when your body starts losing strength
articles.summary: A 47-year study has uncovered a surprising turning point in physical aging: fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among people who exercise regularly. articles.title: Cancer is rising in younger adults, and scientists can't fully explain why
articles.summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved. articles.title: Scientists reveal why some workout recovery tricks can backfire
